name: Isavuconazole
executiveSummary: Triazole (Cresemba) for invasive aspergillosis and mucormycosis. Adult: load **372 mg isavuconazonium (= 200 mg isavuconazole) every 8 h × 6 doses**, then **372 mg (= 200 mg) every 24 h**. In-line filter mandatory.
indications:
## Indications

- Invasive aspergillosis.
- Mucormycosis (alternative to lipid AmB depending on context).

## Precautions

- IV infusion **≥60 min** with **0.2–1.2 µm** filter. No bolus.
- CYP3A4 interactions (potent inducers often contraindicated).
- May **shorten** QTc (unlike many azoles) — still review concomitant drugs.

> Labels saying “200 mg” mean isavuconazole; equals **372 mg** isavuconazonium sulfate.

adulto.presentation: Vial 372 mg isavuconazonium sulfate (= 200 mg isavuconazole); capsules 100 mg isavuconazole (186 mg isavuconazonium).
adulto.dose: Load: **372 mg IV/PO every 8 h × 6 doses** (48 h). Maintenance: **372 mg every 24 h**. (Equals **200 mg** isavuconazole per dose.)
adulto.administration: IV: reconstitute 5 mL SW; dilute in 250 mL NS/D5W; **60 min** with filter. Swallow capsules whole.
adulto.notes: Do not infuse undiluted concentrate by syringe alone per label.

pediatrico.dose: ≥1 year: per weight band on the label. Orientative: ≥18 kg often matches adult (**372 mg**); <18 kg **mg/kg** per SmPC — pediatric ID.
pediatrico.administration: IV/PO with IV filter as adult.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted: ~1 h room temp.
- Diluted: ~6 h room temp / ~24 h refrigerated.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, ↑ transaminases, hypokalemia, headache, infusion reactions.
